title: Score de saignement de Glasgow-Blatchford (GBS)
formula: Addition des points attribués, comme ci-dessous.

how_to_use.why:
- Easy and quick to calculate.
- Doesn’t rely on endoscopic findings.
- Aids in efficient resource utilization.
- Spares the use of NG lavage.
- Scores correlate with cost and length of stay, need for blood transfusion, endoscopic treatment, surgery, and mortality.
- Well-validated in numerous populations.
- Variables such as age, creatinine, coagulopathy, mental status, and comorbidities like malignancy or pulmonary disease are not a part of this calculator, although they may impact medical decision making. Other risk assessment tools like the Rockall and AIMS65 scores account for these variables.
- Has been found to be superior to the AIMS65 in predicting need for intervention (transfusion, endoscopic treatment, IR, or surgery) or rebleeding, although the AIMS65 remains a better predictor of mortality ([Stanley 2017](https://www.bmj.com/content/356/bmj.i6432.long)).
how_to_use.when:
- À utiliser chez les patients adultes chez qui une hospitalisation est envisagée en raison d’une hémorragie digestive haute.
- NE PAS utiliser chez les patients pédiatriques ou chez les patients présentant une suspicion d’hémorragie de l’intestin grêle ou digestive basse.
- Son utilisation est controversée chez les patients déjà hospitalisés, car très peu étaient représentés dans la cohorte originale et beaucoup de ces patients bénéficient d’une évaluation endoscopique.
how_to_use.pearls:
- The Glasgow-Blatchford Bleeding Score (GBS) helps identify which patients with upper GI bleeding (UGIB) may be safely discharged from the emergency room.
- Any of the 9 variables, if present, increase the priority for admission (and likelihood of need for acute intervention).
- Scores range from 0-23, with higher scores corresponding to increasing acuity and mortality.
- A score of 0 suggests low risk of complications (0.5%) and these patients may likely not need to be admitted for workup.
- Scores >0 do not imply that the patient *must* be admitted.
- Clinicians must use their best judgment in assessing whether the patient has heart failure or liver disease. For example, a mild elevation in liver enzymes or steatosis is not considered hepatic failure; likewise, mild diastolic dysfunction was not considered heart failure in the model.
- History of coffee-ground emesis is NOT counted in the tool as it has a low risk of case fatality (likelihood ratio 0.5).

**Points to keep in mind:**

- Clinicians must use their best judgment in assessing whether the patient has heart failure or liver disease. For example, a mild elevation in liver enzymes or steatosis is not considered hepatic failure; likewise, mild diastolic dysfunction was not considered heart failure in the model. History of coffee-ground emesis is NOT counted in the tool as it has a low risk of case fatality (likelihood ratio 0.5).
- Its use is controversial for patients already admitted, as very few were represented in the original cohort and many of these patients receive endoscopic evaluation.
- Variables such as age, creatinine, coagulopathy, mental status, and comorbidities like malignancy or pulmonary disease are not a part of this calculator, although they may impact medical decision making. Other risk assessment tools like the Rockall and AIMS65 Scores account for these variables.

next_steps.advice: Once the decision for admission has been made, efforts should focus on stratifying patients into high and low risk categories to determine which patients need ICU admission and urgent endoscopy.
next_steps.management: La prise en charge initiale doit toujours être axée sur la réanimation hémodynamique avant la stratification du risque.

evidence:
- Modélisé à l'origine dans une population écossaise en 1997, le score de Glasgow-Blatchford est un système de score répandu et bien validé pour les hémorragies digestives hautes.
- De nombreuses études démontrent une meilleure sensibilité que les scores de Rockall pré-endoscopique et complet et que d'autres systèmes validés ([Pang 2010](https://www.giejournal.org/article/S0016-5107(10)00042-8/abstract),[Laursen 2012](https://www.cghjournal.org/article/S1542-3565(12)00786-0/abstract)).
- Le [score AIMS65](nabda:calc.aims65-score-upper-gi-bleeding-mortality) est un système plus récent et plus simple (albumine, INR >1.5, altération de l'état mental, PAS <90, âge = 65) dérivé d'une base de données de population beaucoup plus large. Il est conçu pour prédire la mortalité ([Saltzman 2011](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0016510711018633)).
- Le GBS modifié a des performances similaires et ne prend en compte que le pouls, la pression artérielle, le BUN et l'hémoglobine ([Cheng 2012](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/apt.12029/full)).
- Bien que l'étude originale ait conclu que seuls les scores de 0 permettaient une sortie en toute sécurité, de nombreux essais ultérieurs, dont Stanley et al ([2017](https://www.bmj.com/content/356/bmj.i6432.long)), ont montré que les scores GBS de 1 sont également à faible risque.

**Low risk = Score of 0. Any score higher than 0 is high risk for needing intervention: transfusion, endoscopy, or surgery.**
short_description: Identifie les hémorragies digestives hautes à faible risque.
medium_description: Stratifies upper GI saignement patients who are "faible-risque" et candidates pour ambulatoire prise en charge.
